A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PrITTI with the same authors and core framework. All 26 pages of v1 and 40 pages of v2, including their appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original KITTI-360 reconstruction and generation experiments, synthetic parameterization ablations, and qualitative editing results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional evaluations of PDD and XCube, including hierarchical generation and qualitative extrapolation comparisons.

M1.justification: The hybrid representation, separate ground/object VAE branches, Cholesky encoding, matching losses, diffusion transformer, and RePaint-based editing procedures remain unchanged. Expanded reconstruction and outpainting explanations document the existing method rather than introduce new components.

E1.justification: Both versions use KITTI-360 and synthetic vehicle primitives for the same reconstruction, generation, editing, outpainting, and street-view synthesis tasks. Iterative extrapolation already appears in v1. Other datasets mentioned in v2 describe prior work, not additional datasets evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates SemCity as its external baseline. v2 adds XCube to reconstruction and both PDD and XCube to generation and sampling-sensitivity comparisons, plus PDD to large-scale extrapolation. SemCity 'Base' in v1 matches 'SemCity-1M' in v2; that rename is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: The main generation evaluation switches from a 10 m reference-pose threshold, yielding 3,855 samples, to 1,000 farthest-pose samples, a setting previously explored in v1's appendix. Added hierarchical comparisons introduce level-specific resolutions, upsampling controls, training budgets, and cumulative generation timing. The KITTI-360 train/test split remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The original architecture ablations and sampling-sensitivity study remain, with the latter extended to PDD and XCube. v2 adds substantial analyses of hierarchical refinement, good and poor BEV generations, and extrapolation coherence against PDD, including Figures 13, 16–19, and 24–25.

E5.justification: Both appendices report five random seeds for synthetic dataset generation and average the parameterization ablation results across seeds. The corresponding shaded plot is retained. Neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates or significance tests for the main generation comparisons.

E6.justification: v2 adds XCube reconstruction results and per-level PDD/XCube generation, memory, and timing entries. Main-table generation values also change: DiT-B FID is 55.041 in v1 Table 1 and 73.952 in v2 Table 3, under different reference sampling, so this is not a same-setting deterioration. Existing reconstruction and architecture-ablation table values are retained.

T1.justification: The scatter-matrix construction, symmetry and positive-definiteness reasoning, Cholesky recovery, loss formulations, diffusion equations, and precision/recall definitions are mathematically unchanged. Separately displaying the Cholesky factorization and expanding explanatory prose do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The three methodological contributions remain unchanged. The abstract broadens the empirical claim from outperforming one voxel baseline with up to threefold memory savings to state-of-the-art generation with lower memory, faster inference, and greater editability than voxel-based methods. The conclusion similarly extends the comparison to multiple baselines.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving SemCity's query-sampling mismatch and triplane consistency, and PDD's refinement and split-scene generation. Appendix G newly identifies fixed semantic categories, absent hard geometric constraints, and outpainting seams as limitations. The explicit single-dataset limitation is replaced by discussion of dataset availability and potential applicability elsewhere.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix D and Table 7 document baseline hierarchies, resolutions, training durations, and GPU counts; Section 4.2 newly specifies balanced vegetation conditioning. The abstract explicitly reports public code and models, whereas v1 only supplies a project link. Earlier dataset/software license disclosures and the 300-versus-18-epoch comparison are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds SPAGHETTI and SALAD to distinguish object-part generation from instance-based scene layouts, and introduces a substantial 3D Scene Generation discussion covering geometry, appearance, and panoramic approaches. It also acknowledges sparse-voxel memory efficiency and more explicitly positions PrITTI around semantic control rather than appearance fidelity.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around urban simulation needs, and the abstract, method descriptions, and experimental discussion are substantially revised. The appendix gains separate baseline and precision/recall sections and reorganizes implementation details. These narrative changes extend well beyond inserting new results; the title also adds 'Urban'.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Former combined reconstruction and ablation figures are separated into tables and figures, with revised highlighting and expanded comparisons. New extrusion and latent-outpainting diagrams accompany extensive generation and editing galleries; several earlier qualitative panels are retained or rearranged.

improvement.justification: The documented PDD and sparse-XCube comparisons substantially address v1's reliance on SemCity when arguing for primitives over voxel representations. Hierarchical analyses, good and poor examples, clearer implementation explanations, and additional limitations make the evidence more assessable. The stronger abstract claims still rest on KITTI-360, and changed reference sampling prevents interpreting headline score differences as performance gains, but these limits do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
